Why there's not {a} ~> {c}?

The lax ones are the cases that when the `from` are nulls, the `to` can be any value.
So there's only `c ~> a`.

```
 a | c 
---|---
 1 | 1 
 1 | NULL 
```
Do you mean this case doesn't make a {a} ~> {c} lax FD?

Yes, for a more general situation.
We are maintainly generating the funcdep from:
- Projection
- Index constraint of the table.
- The aggregation.

For case#2, we're curious about whether the from side(the keys) can be null or not. For case#3, we know whether the group-by items can be null or not.

For case#1, we can regard the project as `(x, y, ...z) to f(x, y, ...z)`. We are easy to know whether the `(x, y, ...z)` is null or not, but not easy to know the `f` is null or not. 

So we only consider the from side.

It's possible, but not that useful.

  t(a,b) left join t1(c,d,e) on t.a = t1.c and b=1
   a  b  |  c     d     e
------+----------------
1  1     |  1    NULL   1
1  2     | NULL  NULL  NULL
2  1     | NULL  NULL  NULL

Actually it's possible, only way of the lax FD {a} -> {c} can be derived is in outer join like above but not that useful, let name it as LAX-2. we only maintain the {c} ~> {a} LAX-1 for existence after outer join for now. We also maintain a two Cond-FD (FD can be true but require some condition) {a}=={c} and {}->{b} on the condition that there some predicate can refuse null from at least one of the {c,d,e} in the upper layer selection or other operator. And this seems more useful than introduce of LAX-2. By the way, LAX-2 is bad for do some optimization like FD-Imply.
